newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU moving toward 2003 postal liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU moving toward 2003 postal liberalisation.

text.p: European Union post ministers were moving towards agreement on Wednesday on a plan for opening up EU postal services to competition that would delay significant liberalisation until 2003, EU officials said.

Most countries appeared ready to accept a text that would ask the EU to decide at the start of 2001 whether to abolish state postal monopolies over cross-border mail and direct or "junk" mail, in 2003, they said.
The ministers had previously been deadlocked over how quickly to open up those two sectors. EU leaders at a weekend summit meeting in Dublin ordered them to find a solution by the end of the year.
The European Commission, which had been pushing for a quick liberalisation timetable, agreed to be flexible on Wednesday, which should help ministers reach an accord, officials said.
The ministers would have to agree a plan unanimously rather than by majority if the Commission objected.

Governments have been divided between a Franco-German camp that does not want to set a firm date for opening direct and cross-border mail to competition and an Anglo-Nordic bloc that wants a clear timetable.
The pro-liberalisation camp was unhappy with the text that appeared to be winning favour, EU officials said.

France, wary of a plan that could produce big job losses and incite public unrest, has lobbied heavily for a go-slow. It won surprise support from Germany, which said it was supporting Paris out of a sense of solidarity even though it planned to liberalise its own postal sector.
